newsitem.title: CANADA: MacMillan to sell shipping unit.
newsitem.headline: MacMillan to sell shipping unit.

text.p: Forest products concern MacMillan Bloedel Ltd said Monday it reached a deal to sell its wholly owned shipping unit to Northern Navigation International Inc for C$108 million.
MacMillan said the move was part of an effort to focus on its core businesses and it plans to use the proceeds primarily to pay down debt.

The shipping division is called Canadian Transport Co Ltd and is headquartered in Barbados. It owns five open-hatch gantry-craned specialized ships for handling forest products. The sale is expected to close by the end of March.
As part of the sale, MacMillan entered long-term exclusive contracts with the firm to transport its cargoes to Japan and Europe.

Canadian Transport, which has 42 employees, provides twice monthly forest products service from British Columbia to Japan, a monthly forest products service from the Pacific Northwest to northern Europe and a monthly service carrying steel and general cargo from Europe to the North American west coast.
Northern Navigation, with offices in Connecticut, Seattle and Oslo, has a fleet of 15 ships, most of which are forest products carriers.
In 1996, Canadian Transport carried more than 1.6 million tonnes of cargo.
